mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single inter-regional authentication under the Mainland-HK arrangement: (a) notarisation by a Hong Kong Notary Public; (b) attestation by a China-Appointed Attesting Officer; (c) verification stamp by China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited. Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization are not applicable to this Mainland-HK document flow and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Standing) of the Hong Kong Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same single inter-regional route as the Certificate of Incorporation, consisting exclusively of Hong Kong notarisation, China-Appointed Attesting Officer certification, and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited endorsement; no Apostille or Consular chain is to be appended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing establishment of the PRC WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution witnessed by a Hong Kong Notary Public, followed by China-Appointed Attesting Officer certification and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited confirmation. This is a mutually exclusive alternative to both Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization and must not be chained with either.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Hong Kong Parent Company (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Solicitor / Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a HKSAR solicitor; then the same Mainland-HK notarisation route as above. In case the parent entity relies on third-country documentation, the sole permissible alternative is Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the Apostille member state where the document resides; consular legalization is not added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Hong Kong Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: HSBC Holdings plc or other qualifying bank (United Kingdom, Hague Apostille member)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route exclusively: (a) notarisation by a UK notary public (if the bank deems it necessary); (b) single Apostille certificate issued by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. The PRC authorities receive the Apostille directly; no Chinese Consular Legalization is performed or appended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors / Shareholders extract of the Hong Kong Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Registered Agent or Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the registered agent, then treated under the Mainland-HK notarisation arrangement: Hong Kong notary notarisation, China-Appointed Attesting Officer attestation, and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited certification. This route is reserved for Mainland China use; the Hague Apostille is not used for this flow and no consular legalization applies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory screening protocol for the Hong Kong parent and all identified UBOs is a layered, risk-based CDD exercise under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2024 revision) and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3. Every natural person UBO at or above the 25% threshold, all directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and the Consolidated Sanctions List of the UN Security Council (including the 1267/1988 Al-Qaida/ISIL regime), the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the HKSAR sanctions lists maintained under the United Nations Sanctions Ordinance (Cap 537), the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, and adverse media/politically exposed persons (PEP) databases in the jurisdictions of tax residence and citizenship. Substantive verification of the UBO name and address must be completed with passport copies, proof of address, and corporate ownership charts. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered by PEP status, a high-risk residency country, or any watch-list hit; negative screening findings must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and halt incorporation until clearing. Continuous monitoring is required post-incorporation at least on every anniversary and upon any ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Pre-Approval System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Registration Online Platform (zwfw.samr.gov.cn) and local municipal Market Supervision Administration portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Chinese character name structured in four tiers: administrative division + trade name + industry/organization characteristic + enterprise form (e.g., [City] [Trade Name] International Trading Co., Ltd.). The trade name must be distinct within the same administrative region and industry; English names may be registered in Pinyin or a permitted transliteration but the Chinese name is the binding legal name under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR Decree No. 34). Foreign trade names require a transliteration in Chinese, and no English-only or alphabet-only names are acceptable for the WFOE.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a formal rejection notice from the SAMR enterprise name registration portal, the applicant (or the appointed incorporation agent) may file a written administrative reconsideration application with the next superior Market Supervision Administration within 15 working days of the rejection, citing supporting law under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may initiate an administrative litigation before the competent People's Court within 6 months. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately re-file a new name containing a different trade name while the appeal is pending. Any name reservation set to expire must be extended or re-filed not fewer than 5 working days prior to expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a trading WFOE, virtual office arrangements are largely impermissible as a primary registered address. A commercial mail-forwarding address may satisfy the correspondence aspect in some cities, but the PRC tax authorities and the opening bank will require a physical lease in the name of the WFOE, an office premises use certificate, and on-site presence commensurate with wholesale trading operations. Herbal export business (ISIC 4631) is treated as requiring verifiable commercial substance; pure virtual offices are rejected in practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantifiable risk of unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months is estimated at 55-70% for a newly incorporated export WFOE in ISIC 4631. Checklist for compliance readiness: (1) physical office signage in Chinese corresponding to the registered name; (2) employees present at normal business hours; (3) signed lease agreement, property tax receipts and management fee invoices available on-site; (4) accounting vouchers, contracts, import-export records and Goji berry procurement traceability logs; (5) business license framed and displayed; (6) customs declaration receipts aligned with SWIFT/TT payment flows; (7) origin-maintenance of the registered address for all regulatory correspondence. Municipal tax authorities and SAMR may inspect without prior notice where any invoice/export anomaly is flagged; non-occupancy triggers disqualification of the address and revocation of the registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 5, 10, 11, 14, 15, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29, 31, 32, 33, 35, 42, 47, 73, 74 and 86; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020), Articles 4, 11, 12, and 30; Interim Provisions on the Registration and Administration of Market Entities issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (2022); and Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) 2022 Edition.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Municipal or Provincial Market Supervision Administration where the WFOE registered address is located, acting through the Enterprise Registration Section of the Government Service Center or the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company together with the notarized Articles of Association and the supporting corporate documents of the Hong Kong shareholder.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for an ordinary WFOE under the PRC Company Law 2023. The articles of association must state a subscribed registered capital, and all subscribed capital must be fully paid in within five years from the date of establishment unless the articles adopt a shorter period. The Hong Kong shareholder must open a domestic capital account or foreign currency capital account through a designated bank and remit contributions in accordance with the foreign investment information reporting rules. No blocked escrow account is required for the wholesale and export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, as this activity is not on the foreign investment negative list. The bank, customs, and export food registration procedures may require evidence of paid-in capital and working capital sufficient to support the committed export volume.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] DRIED GOJI HERBAL EXPORT WFOE LIMITED
A wholly foreign-owned enterprise organized under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China.
DATE: ______________ PLACE: ______________
WHEREAS, the sole shareholder [Name of Hong Kong Parent, Hong Kong registration number] has approved the formation of the Company as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company for the international bulk wholesale and export of organic dried Lycium barbarum and herbal botanicals under ISIC 4631, and has executed the Articles of Association;
WHEREAS, the registered capital of the Company shall be fixed in the Articles of Association and shall be contributed by the sole shareholder in accordance with the term prescribed by the PRC Company Law, which term shall not exceed five years unless an earlier date is approved by the sole shareholder;
WHEREAS, the lawful establishment of the Company requires the adoption of a registered office, the appointment of statutory officers, the opening of banking facilities, and the authorization of management to complete all statutory registrations and industrial licensing filings;
NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED:
1. INCORPORATION AND SHARE CAPITAL. That the Company be and is hereby established as a limited liability company under the laws of the People's Republic of China. The authorized capital shall be [amount in RMB] divided into [number] ordinary shares with a par value of [amount] RMB each. The subscription of the sole shareholder to all such shares is accepted, and the capital contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Association is approved. The legal representative and the general manager shall collect all contributions, issue share certificates, update the shareholder register, and cause all statutory capital contribution records to be filed with the local Market Supervision Administration.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE. That the registered office of the Company shall be at [full address], being a verifiable legal address within the jurisdiction of the local Market Supervision Administration. The officers of the Company are authorized to execute an office lease, post the legal address plaque, complete the property use filing, and maintain the register of members and statutory books at that address.
3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. That the management of the Company is authorized to open a basic deposit account, a general deposit account, and a foreign currency capital account at one or more licensed banks in China or Hong Kong, and to maintain Swift TT and wire transfer facilities. All account signatories shall be designated in a bank mandate, and no payment from corporate accounts shall be made without the joint signature of the legal representative and the general manager or the legal representative and the supervisor, subject to the limits stated in a separate written mandate.
4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. That [Name] is appointed legal representative, [Name] is appointed supervisor, and [Name] is appointed general manager, each to serve until removed by a subsequent resolution. The legal representative shall represent the Company before the Market Supervision Administration, tax authorities, customs, banks, and all courts and tribunals, and may not delegate such authority except by a written instrument approved by the sole shareholder.
5. REGULATORY FILINGS AND LICENSING. That all officers and the corporate secretary are directed to prepare, sign, and submit all forms and to engage notaries, lawyers, accountants, and agents necessary to complete company registration, tax registration, social insurance, foreign exchange, statistics, customs registration, export food enterprise registration, food business licensing, and foreign trade operator filing, and to re-file whenever the business scope, capital, officers, registered address, or banking mandate is changed.
6. EFFECTIVE DATE. That these resolutions are effective immediately upon adoption, shall be entered in the official minute book, and shall be binding on the Company. Any preparatory acts performed before this date in anticipation of incorporation are hereby ratified and confirmed.
ADOPTED this ____ day of _______, 20____ at [city], in the presence of two subscribing witnesses.
Chairman or General Manager: [Name]
Supervisor: [Name]
Corporate Secretary: [Name]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Autonomous Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration online service hall, Enterprise Name Autonomous Declaration System on the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the electronic registration system of the local Market Supervision Administration and choose the foreign-invested enterprise establishment pathway. Enter up to five proposed names structured as institution name plus industry description plus limited liability company, and verify against the national market entity name database and protected trademarks. Insert the exact business scope corresponding to ISIC 4631: wholesale of edible dried fruits and herbal botanicals, trading and supply chain management, and import and export of goods and technology. Upload the digital identity of the proposed legal representative, submit the application for autonomous name declaration, download the name acceptance certificate, and retain the application reference number for the later formation filing.
required_dossiers: Five proposed company names in Chinese and English transliteration alternatives
Shareholder identity certificate or business registration extract of the Hong Kong parent company
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent and legal representative
Signed undertaking on name integrity and business scope compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the automated name check issues a similarity or objection notice, promptly submit a revised name application through the same online channel, or apply for administrative reconsideration with the local Market Supervision Administration within the statutory period. A suspension caused by incomplete identity verification may be cured within five working days by re-uploading the notarized Hong Kong parent identity documents and a corrected authorization letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Association and Shareholder Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong China-appointed Attesting Officer; Legal Service Department of the Government of the Hong Kong SAR; local Market Supervision Administration preliminary document review desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate package through a Hong Kong notary public appointed under the mainland and Hong Kong arrangement. The sole shareholder must adopt a written resolution approving the incorporation, the capital subscription schedule, and the initial officers. Draft the Articles of Association in Chinese with an English translation, setting out the exact business scope, registered capital, contribution period within five years, the division of authority between the legal representative and general manager, and the bank signing rules. The notarized Hong Kong parent documents, including certificate of incorporation, commercial registration, shareholder register and beneficial ownership declaration, must be certified by a China-appointed attesting officer, and the signature pages of the Articles and shareholder resolution must be executed by the parent board.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation and commercial registration of the Hong Kong shareholder
Certificate of good standing issued by the Hong Kong Companies Registry within six months
Parent board or shareholder resolution authorizing incorporation of the WFOE
Proposed Articles of Association in Chinese with English translation
Appointment instruments for legal representative, supervisor and general manager
Passport or identity card copies of the appointed officers and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary office queries beneficial ownership, file a confirmation declaration and provide the corporate registry search extract. If the local Market Supervision Administration rejects the Articles for inconsistency with model articles, revise the text through a short-form shareholder amendment and resubmit within five working days. If authentication is missing, cure by obtaining the required attesting officer seal and re-filing before the preliminary review deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration, Enterprise Registration Section, through the Government Service Center or the online market entity registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete establishment application through the local government service center or the online market entity registration portal. Submit the approved name certificate, signed Articles of Association, address use proof, notarized parent company documents, and identification of the legal representative, supervisor and manager. The registration officer will check the foreign investment negative list, verify that the business scope is not restricted, and issue a unified social credit code business license. The legal representative must sign the application in person or through a notarized authorization, and must not use the company seal before the license is issued. After issuance, preserve the original business license and file the foreign investment information initial return with the local commerce authority.
required_dossiers: Pre-approved company name certificate
Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Articles of Association signed by the shareholder and all initial members
Registered office use certificate, lease recordation, or ownership evidence with landlord consent
Legal representative identification and passport-style photograph
Supervisor and general manager appointment letters and identity documents
Foreign investment information initial return form
Notarized corporate documents of the Hong Kong shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Market Supervision Administration issues a query, respond within the statutory grace period with a supplemental explanation and corrected forms. If the application is returned because of business scope wording, delete the queried item and resubmit through the online amendment channel. If the proposed legal representative is disqualified, appoint a substitute qualified person and submit a fresh appointment resolution together with the amended registration application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Statutory Seals, Tax, Banking, Customs and Foreign Exchange Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving enterprise; local State Taxation Administration office; General Administration of Customs local branch; State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the designated domestic bank; provincial commerce department for foreign trade operator filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a public security licensed seal engraving unit to produce the company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, invoice seal, and contract seal after presenting the business license. Complete tax registration and information confirmation at the local tax branch, obtain the taxpayer status, open a basic deposit account and a foreign currency capital account at a designated bank, and complete the foreign exchange entity list filing. For the export of dried goji berries, complete the foreign trade operator record with the provincial commerce department, apply for customs registration through the GACC electronic portal, and file the export food enterprise registration with the local customs food safety division before the first shipment. The bank mandate must reflect the two-person signing rule adopted in the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Original business license and copies
Company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal and contract seal approved by the Public Security Bureau
Articles of Association and first board resolution on bank signatories
Legal representative identification and company bank mandate form
Registered office lease and landlord identity records
Foreign investor identification confirmation form
Customs registration application and export food enterprise self-declaration
Tax registration forms, accounting system statement, and bank account information
Foreign trade operator filing form and product standard documentation for dried goji berries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account opening is delayed due to the absence of the legal representative at the callback interview, reschedule the interview or submit a notarized authorization for a senior local manager. If customs rejects the export food enterprise registration because of incomplete food safety documentation, remedy by updating the HACCP-style control plan and resubmitting through the GACC portal. Tax late-filing penalties may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure before the tax authority initiates an inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration Food Business Licensing Division for wholesale food permit; provincial commerce department for foreign trade operator filing; General Administration of Customs and local customs for export food enterprise registration; municipal ecological environment bureau if a new warehouse or processing facility is constructed.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business License for Wholesale of Edible Agricultural Products and Herbal Botanicals; Foreign Trade Operator Filing; GACC Export Food Enterprise Registration; Customs Registration Certificate for the WFOE.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China and the local Ecological Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA triggered for pure wholesale trading and brokerage of dried goji berries. If the enterprise uses an existing third-party warehouse and does not construct new buildings, the activity is outside the 2021 EIA Classification Management List. Construction of a new ordinary dry warehouse may require only an environmental registration form; a full EIA report or environmental impact report form is not required because the goods are non-hazardous dried botanicals.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, boiler, or chemical exhaust is generated by the core wholesale activity. Any domestic sewage must meet local municipal sewer standards. Packaging waste must be sorted and transferred under the Solid Waste Pollution Prevention and Control Law. Hazardous waste, if any from pest control or disinfection, must be stored and transported in compliance with GB 18597-2023 and the national hazardous waste manifest system. If the enterprise later introduces cleaning, fumigation, polishing, or sulfur removal operations, atmospheric emissions must comply with GB 16297-1996: non-methane total hydrocarbons not exceeding 120 mg/m3 in exhaust and 30 mg/m3 at facility boundary. Wastewater generated from such processing must comply with GB 8978-1996: chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 500 mg/L and suspended solids not exceeding 70 mg/L before municipal connection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office and warehouse must obtain a fire safety filing or acceptance certificate from the local fire rescue institution where required under the Fire Control Law and building fire protection regulations. A people's air defense or civil defense permit is not required because the project creates no underground construction or civil-defense obligation. Occupational clearance under the Work Safety Law requires a workplace risk assessment, fire extinguishers, marked emergency exits, emergency evacuation plan, and employee safety training. If racking storage is installed, a registered engineer must certify the structural load capacity of the floor, racks, and shelving.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic portal: China Electronic Taxpayer / Electronic Tax Bureau of State Taxation Administration (https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign investor incorporates the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), obtaining a Business License that automatically carries the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). This USCC is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN/VAT ID) for the WFOE; no separate TIN application is required. Step 2: Under the multi-department joint registration mechanism, SAMR synchronizes registration data in real time to the local tax bureau of the STA, completing basic tax registration. Step 3: Within 30 days of the Business License date, the WFOE must file supplementary taxpayer information through the Electronic Taxpayer Portal, including legal representative, accounting system and software, authorized personnel, bank account reports, and expected VAT taxpayer status (general or small-scale). Step 4: The WFOE must complete the Financial and Accounting System Registration Filing and Bank Deposit Account Filing through the same portal. Step 5: For a foreign non-resident entity with no Chinese establishment but with China-source taxable income, the foreign entity must separately file a Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Registration/Filing with the competent STA branch before payment remittance; the withholding agent files the Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Withholding Return and the foreign entity obtains a local non-resident taxpayer reference number. Step 6: A VAT general taxpayer must implement the digital e-invoice system and obtain the electronic tax seal certificate through the STA platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box regime or hybrid mismatch election for corporate entities. An eligible WFOE may elect to register as a VAT general taxpayer before exceeding the CNY 5,000,000 threshold or may remain a small-scale taxpayer; it may also elect applicable double tax treaty benefits for non-resident withholding rates, but no entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) administered by the State Taxation Administration; exported goods are zero-rated with refund entitlement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold for basic tax registration; every WFOE must register for tax upon Business License issuance. The mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable sales exceeding CNY 5,000,000 (RMB 5 million); below this threshold the entity may be registered as a small-scale taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China's Golden Tax Phase IV and Digital Electronic Invoice mandate require all VAT taxpayers to issue invoices through the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform using real-time fiscal digitalization. Fully digital e-invoices are cleared by the STA in real time; each invoice receives a unique anti-fraud electronic invoice number and is digitally stamped through the integrated tax-control infrastructure. XML/OFD data must be transmitted automatically at issuance; offline or hand-written VAT invoices are not permitted for B2B export transactions. API-based integration is required for high-volume exporters, and all invoice data is centrally captured for export tax-refund matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals by the WFOE are eligible for VAT zero-rating (export exemption and refund) provided the goods physically leave the customs territory of the PRC, are declared to customs under export procedure, the WFOE holds valid taxpayer qualification, the export sales are evidenced by a VAT export invoice, the foreign exchange proceeds are repatriated through a designated foreign-exchange bank, and the exporter passes customs verification of the export declaration, including volume, HS code, valuation, and destination. The buyer must be located outside the PRC customs territory; where the buyer is a related party, transfer pricing documentation must support arm's-length pricing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: PRC Customs Export Goods Declaration processed through the China International Trade Single Window with a Customs Declaration Number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual export shipment
Commercial Invoice issued by the WFOE to the offshore buyer
Packing List corresponding to the Commercial Invoice
Inward Foreign Exchange Settlement/Receipt Voucher issued by a designated foreign-exchange bank showing repatriation of export proceeds
Export Tax Refund Declaration Data filed via the STA Electronic Taxpayer Portal and matched electronically with Customs and banking data
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT refunds are scrutinized through the STA-Customs-People's Bank data reconciliation system. If zero-rating is granted and later found unverified or fraudulent, the tax authority recovers the refunded amount, collects late-payment surcharge, and imposes penalties under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Levies. For fraudulent export-refund claims, the fine ranges from one to five times the refund amount obtained; for general underpayment or unverified claims, a fine of 50% to five times the amount involved may apply. The exporter may also be placed on a tax compliance blacklist, have export tax-refund qualification revoked, and be referred for criminal prosecution for tax fraud. Retrospective clawback is not time-limited for fraud; for ordinary unverified claims the assessment period is generally three years, extending to five years where concealment is found.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, functioning under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the consolidated foreign exchange regulatory and registration authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a bifurcated current/capital account convertibility model. Current account transactions connected to the WFOE's production and trade of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals enjoy very high convertibility once the underlying contract, invoice, customs declaration, and logistics documentation are authenticated by the designated custodian domestic bank. Capital account transactions are subject to strict registration, use and repatriation limitations. Inbound FDI equity contributions must pass through SAFE's registration system, be deposited into a specially designated foreign currency capital account, and may be settled into RMB only after bank-level authenticity screening and the issuance of an FDI capital verification report. Profit remittances to the Hong Kong parent are permissible only after statutory audit, payment of enterprise income tax, and submission of board resolutions, financial statements, tax payment certificates, and audited profit appropriation evidence; banks must verify no historical capital account violation, unpaid foreign debt, or improperly grandfathered settlement. Non-trade current payments, service fees, and royalties may be challenged without economic substance evidence. Overall the RMB remains not freely convertible on the capital account, so all treasury plans must build in regulatory lead time.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from dried goji berry and herbal wholesale transactions must be repatriated to the WFOE's domestic foreign exchange account through the designated bank rather than held offshore. The WFOE is not required to convert export receipts into RMB at a forced ratio; under current-account convertibility the enterprise may retain foreign currency in a settlement account or voluntarily convert at spot rate. The obligatory mechanics are administrative: bank-side collection verification, China Customs and SAFE data matching, and generation of trade settlement and payment records in the unified trade single window. Receipts must be collected within the payment term stated in the sales contract and customs declaration; overdue receipts beyond the bank's risk threshold, normally 90 days or earlier if exceptional false-export indicators are detected, require a signed explanation, amended invoice, collection order, and proof of foreign buyer insolvency or dispute. Any unrepatriated export revenues are flagged as suspected round-tripping or transfer pricing, triggering trade verification audits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-viable for the PRC operative entity. Offshore EMIs, including licensed Hong Kong stored-value facilities, are not recognized as domestic deposit-taking institutions by PBOC or SAFE, and therefore cannot host the WFOE's basic RMB account, receive FDI capital, process trade settlement verification, or execute profit remittance. The Cross-Border RMB clearing and CIPS participation are accessed only through licensed domestic banks. EMIs cannot satisfy the physical presence, corporate seal, or facial biometric identity requirements, and they would cause the WFOE to fail bank status verification and liquidity traceability. Use EMIs solely for non-CNY invoice data or HK parent side treasury syntax, never as a regulated onshore payment rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch attendance is mandatory for the WFOE legal representative during account opening and activation for the FDI capital account; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted. An authorized deputy may appear with a notarized, apostilled or legalized power of attorney, original board resolution, and the legal representative's passport notarial copy; however, most tier-1 banks require at least one legal representative interview. The Hong Kong parent shareholder should provide a certificate of incumbency, Memorandum and Articles of Association, board resolution, and ultimate beneficial owner declarations. Some banks permit a video pre-interview for identity verification, but wet-ink sealed applications, corporate seal control, and branch witness signatures remain mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership anonymity: WFOE is wholly owned by an HK holding company whose shareholders may be personal names, trusts, or nominees; mainland banks view offshore nominee layers as a high-money-laundering trigger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO chart through each legal entity, certified passports, trust deed, letter of wishes if irrevocable trust, audited financial statements of the HK company, Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate, NAR1 annual return, incumbency certificate, director and shareholder register, source of wealth statement, and independent director and beneficial owner declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate capital contribution by HK parent with no demonstrated operating substance: large equity injection into WFOE soon after incorporation with no prior asset base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of remitting parent covering 12 months, invoice or loan documentation if funds arise from operations, sale of equity, dividend vouchers, tax assessment, source-of-wealth statement from beneficial owners, board resolution of HK parent and WFOE approving the investment, and a coherent business plan for goji berry and herbal procurement plus international sale contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade mismatch and herbal product misclassification: declared price or quantity inconsistent with market index for dried Lycium barbarum, or HS code mismatch with botanical supplements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE trade monitoring system record, purchase contracts with PRC growers or cooperatives, VAT invoice, customs export declarations, weight and packing list, phytosanitary certificate, inspection and quarantine certificate, third-party laboratory analysis for heavy metals, sulphur and pesticides, marine bill of lading or air waybill, insurance certificate, and bank collection schedule matching payment amounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargoes or final destination ambiguity: goji and raw herbal consignments sold through HK broker with redirection to sensitive jurisdictions or military or narcotics end-user risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and sanctions screening report from a reputable compliance database on all counterparties, signed end-user certificate or sales contract prohibiting re-export to embargoed destinations, license to export plant products and any export license under PRC Foreign Trade Law, country-of-origin certificate, compliance attestation that products are food and beverage raw material not controlled dual-use items, and a cascade audit trail from HK broker to final customs entry.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route parent HK funds by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to WFOE's foreign currency capital account; applicant and beneficiary must match SAFE registration, and the payment narrative should reference FDI equity contribution plus the unique FDI foreign exchange registration number. The designated bank verifies authenticity with the SAFE digital system, records the foreign exchange settlement declaration, then converts into RMB for operating purposes; after the contribution, an authorized PRC CPA must issue a capital verification report confirming paid-in capital. The proceeds may not be used for equity investments, securities, loans to shareholders, or non-operating real estate without further approval. If the parent contributes in RMB from Hong Kong, the remitting bank must handle RMB clearing through CIPS with a CN RMB payment reason and an RCPMIS reporting obligation; the recommended path is foreign-currency injection followed by onshore settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade disbursements to global goji berry buyers and suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 for urgent telegraphic transfers with precise purpose of payment codes tied to commodity sale or purchase; for documentary LCs under UCP600 for bulk high-value quantities; and documentary collections under URC522 for open-account or consignment flows. Each outbound remittance must be matched with export and import supporting vouchers, customs declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and insurance certificate. For RMB cross-border settlement, use CIPS or a designated clearing bank; for USD, clear through the correspondent network into the WFOE's CNY account and then settle against the invoice. The bank will apply trade verification and potential post-shipment finance checks; internal conversion from CNY to USD for disbursement requires a spot FX purpose code and underlying trade documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB and USD forward contracts with a qualified mainstream bank, allowed only for genuine current-account trade exposure supported by contract and purchase orders; the hedge must mature within the trade horizon and cannot be speculative.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not executable directly by the PRC WFOE; the HK parent treasury may layer them offshore to buffer CNY volatility, provided the WFOE remains contractually isolated from synthetic CNY derivative settlement.

Currency swaps with a licensed Chinese bank may be permissible on a real-demand principle for conversion of foreign currency liabilities and equity-related cashflows, requiring SAFE or bank approval and documented exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation of the WFOE; due once every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee escalates to HKD 870 (approx USD 111.54) if delivered after 42 days but not more than 3 months; HKD 1,740 (approx USD 223.08) if over 3 months but not more than 6 months; HKD 2,610 (approx USD 334.62) if over 6 months but not more than 12 months; HKD 3,480 (approx USD 446.15) if over 12 months. Continued non-compliance may trigger Companies Registry prosecution and administrative strike-off under section 744 of the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal and payment of Business Registration Fee and Levy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal is due annually within one month after expiry of the certificate; the IRD Renewal Demand Note specifies the exact due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a late penalty of HKD 300 (approx USD 38.46); continued failure to renew may lead to prosecution, fines up to HKD 5,000, and cancellation of the Business Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Profits Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The return is generally issued on the first working day of April for corporations; filing is due within one month of issuance for non-tax-agent cases, and extended to 15 August of the same year of assessment for due-filing agents where the accounting period ends on 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the schedule incurs a late filing penalty of up to HKD 10,000 (approx USD 1,282.05); subsequent failure may lead to estimated assessments, additional penalties, and prosecution. Repeated non-compliance may attract penalties up to three times the amount of tax ultimately assessed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A with IR56B forms) for all employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued on 1 April or the first working day of April annually; filing is due within one month after the issue date for corporate employers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing may incur penalties up to HKD 10,000 (approx USD 1,282.05) per offence; persistent failure may lead to prosecution and estimated salaries tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements approved by directors and submitted as part of the Profits Tax Return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and retained at the registered office for shareholder inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must approve and sign the financial statements within 6 months after the financial year-end; the audit must be completed and the accounts submitted together with the BIR51 within the IRD filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to audit and file audited accounts exposes the company and each responsible officer to a fine of up to HKD 300,000 (approx USD 38,461.54) and potential strike-off; the auditor's report must state whether the financial statements give a true and fair view under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance and update of the Significant Controllers Register (SCR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with any government body; register and supporting documents must be kept at the WFOE's registered office and made available for inspection by the Companies Registry and designated law enforcement agencies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The SCR must be accurate at all times and updated within 7 days of any change in significant controllers; no separate annual UBO filing is required to be lodged with the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep a compliant SCR is an offence punishable by a fine at Level 4 (HKD 25,000, approx USD 3,205.13) and, for continuing default, a daily default fine of HKD 700 (approx USD 89.74).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Hong Kong does not provide size-based audit exemptions by balance-sheet total, annual turnover, or headcount. A WFOE that carries on any significant accounting transaction is legally required to undergo an independent audit by a certified public accountant under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) sections 404-408. For this trading entity, the triggering thresholds are effectively: annual revenue or turnover exceeding HKD 0, balance-sheet total exceeding HKD 0, and any employees above zero, because any such activity disqualifies dormant-company status. A company is dormant only if it has no significant accounting transactions; the instant WFOE's international bulk export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals will always exceed this threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), generally converged with IFRS; eligible private companies may apply the Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standard for Private Entities (HKFRS for Private Entities); statutory financial statements are prepared in accordance with Schedule 10 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and are adjusted for tax computation in the Profits Tax Return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of UBO/shareholder information is achieved through filing the Annual Return (NAR1) with the Companies Registry, which must contain a complete list of members and shareholdings as at the anniversary date of incorporation. Share transfers must be submitted to the company, documented in the Register of Members, and the resulting change in registered ownership must be reflected in the NAR1 filed for the next annual return date. In parallel, any significant controller holding 25% or more of the voting rights, possessing the power to appoint or remove a majority of the board, or otherwise exercising significant influence must be recorded in the Significant Controllers Register within 7 days of the change. No annual UBO confirmation is separately filed with the Companies Registry, but the SCR and underlying inspection records must be preserved at the registered office for statutory inspections.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$400 - US$1,200 per year for registered office address and company secretary service; higher if a professional corporate secretarial firm prepares minutes and NAR1 filings, typically up to US$1,800
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500 - US$6,000 per annum depending on transaction volume, inventory complexity, and foreign-currency export flows of the goji berry wholesale business

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China's Small Low-Profit Enterprise regime (annual taxable income <= RMB 3 million, employees <= 300, total assets <= RMB 50 million) applies a 20% reduced rate on a 25% taxable base, yielding an effective 5% rate for qualifying entities; High and New Technology Enterprises pay a 15% rate; qualifying R&D expenses enjoy a 100% additional deduction; no general patent box applies to herbal wholesale, but certain agricultural product processing and encouraged regional incentives may be available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (A Class), together with related schedules such as A105000, A105080, A107041 and the annual Related Party Transactions Reporting Schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system (e-Tax) or the provincial electronic tax bureau portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation with quarterly provisional CIT advance payments; quarterly prepayment returns are filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter and the annual return is filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return and final settlement must be filed by 31 May of the year following the tax year; quarterly provisional returns must be filed by the 15th day immediately following each quarter-end; if the due date falls on a statutory holiday, the deadline is automatically extended to the next working day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue recognized from the international wholesale export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, including all export sales under FOB, CIF, and CFR trade terms, converted at the PBOC central parity rate; exclude VAT zero-rated export turnover and export rebate receivables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross foreign-currency remittances from the Hong Kong parent or intermediary buyer net of bank charges; reconcile recognized revenue with customs declarations, bills of lading, sales contracts, and Swift TT receipts; transfer-pricing adjustments must be considered if the intercompany price deviates from comparable uncontrolled export prices of dried goji berries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct procurement costs of raw dried lycium and herbal botanicals, packaging materials, quality inspection, phytosanitary treatment, fumigation, direct labor, utilities, and production or processing overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE purchases agricultural raw materials from related parties in Hong Kong or elsewhere, the purchase price must satisfy the arm's length standard and be supported by supplier invoices, agricultural acquisition vouchers, cost allocation records, and a benchmark analysis; inflated agricultural invoice purchases are a classic audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty, property tax, land-use tax, vehicle and vessel tax, and other taxes and surcharges recorded as current-period expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export sales of dried goji berries are VAT zero-rated or exempt, so no output VAT is recognized on overseas shipments; input VAT must be allocated between exportable and domestic sales; stamp duty applies to cross-border purchase and sale contracts at the statutory rate; under-accrual of surcharges will distort taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ocean freight, marine insurance, customs brokerage, foreign-trade documentation fees, trade-show expenses, international buyer travel, marketing and advertising costs, and sales personnel salaries and social insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to the Hong Kong parent or affiliated logistics firms for freight, insurance, or agency services must demonstrate actual service provision and business benefit; related-party service charges are deductible only to the extent they satisfy the arm's length benefit test; any duplicate or shareholder-level selling overhead will be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management and head-office salaries, professional legal and accounting fees, office rent, utilities, stationery, depreciation, repairs, and corporate governance expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, brand licence fees, or head-office cost allocations charged by the Hong Kong parent to the WFOE are deductible only if the services were actually rendered, the WFOE received a direct and demonstrable benefit, and the amount is at arm's length; pure shareholder costs are non-deductible and may be reclassified as disguised dividend distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bank interest on domestic and cross-border borrowings, intercompany loan interest, foreign exchange losses, bank handling fees, letter-of-credit charges, and other financing expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the Hong Kong parent must observe the thin capitalization debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises; excess interest is non-deductible and may be re-characterized as dividends subject to 10% or treaty-reduced 7% WHT; foreign-exchange losses must be realized and properly documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7 - Investment Gains / Fair Value Changes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gains or losses from equity investments, financial instruments, derivative contracts, and fair-value re-measurement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any capital transaction with the Hong Kong parent, such as share transfers or quasi-equity advances, must be reported on the related party transaction schedules; transfers of shares or financial assets between related parties at non-arm's length values will be adjusted under CIT Law Article 41.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 1 less Lines 2 through 6 plus Line 7, representing the operating profit of the WFOE before non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The operating profit margin and Berry Ratio of a wholesale herbal exporter should be compared with publicly listed distributors and wholesale traders; a persistent low or negative margin while the Hong Kong parent earns high margins will trigger transfer-pricing audit and special tax adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Government grants, compensation income, asset surplus gains, and other income outside ordinary wholesale operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export subsidies, price subsidies, and agricultural support grants received by the WFOE are includible unless an explicit CIT exemption applies; failure to declare subsidies received in foreign currency from Hong Kong or offshore sources may lead to tax evasion allegations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Charitable donations, fines, penalties, non-performing asset losses, inventory spoilage losses, and losses from asset disposal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Administrative fines, tax late-payment surcharges, and illegal expenses are non-deductible; charitable donations are deductible only if made through qualifying public welfare organizations and within 12% of annual accounting profit; physical loss of dried goji goods must be evidenced by customs, insurance, or independent survey reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The accounting total profit adjusted for all schedule additions and reductions, yielding the CIT taxable income before loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule A105000 to add back non-deductible entertainment, advertising, fines, and related-party charges disallowed under the arm's length and benefit rules; loss carryforward is limited to five years; the taxable profit must be consistent with the transfer-pricing policy maintained for the Hong Kong parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 / Line 12 - Tax Payable and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at 25% (or the applicable preferential rate) less quarterly prepayments, foreign tax credits, and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise and pays CIT at 25% on worldwide income; dividends distributed to the Hong Kong parent are not deductible at the WFOE level and are not taxed again in the WFOE return; rather, they attract withholding tax at the payment level under CIT Law Article 37 and the China-Hong Kong DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 / Related Party Transaction Disclosure Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all cross-border related-party transactions with the Hong Kong parent, including sale of dried goji berries, procurement, logistics, management services, interest, royalties, and share transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing is mandatory whenever related-party transactions exist; include each controlled transaction's amount, pricing policy, TP method applied, and benchmark selection; failure to disclose or prepare contemporaneous documentation triggers investigation and penalties, and the burden of proof may shift to the taxpayer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 62: formal warning or fine up to RMB 2,000, increased up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; late payment surcharge accrues at 0.05% per day on unpaid tax under Article 32; underpayment due to false filing attracts 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid; intentional tax evasion in excess of RMB 50,000 and 10% of the tax due constitutes criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, carrying imprisonment up to 7 years, fines, and forfeiture.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by the Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise under CIT Law Article 37; the rate is reduced to 5% under the Mainland and Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Arrangement, Article 10, if the Hong Kong shareholder is the beneficial owner and directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's share capital; otherwise the full 10% applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Hong Kong shareholder must first obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department (commonly via Form IR1313A) for the calendar year covering the dividend payment. Second, the WFOE must prepare a Beneficial Ownership Self-Assessment and a complete ownership-chain file showing direct 25% shareholding, board minutes approving the dividend, financial statements of the Hong Kong shareholder, and evidence of real economic substance in Hong Kong. Third, before remitting the dividend, the withholding agent must submit a non-resident tax treaty benefit application through the competent Chinese tax bureau or online tax portal, together with the Tax Residency Certificate, notarized/certified corporate registration, beneficial ownership declaration, and confirmation that the Hong Kong shareholder does not have a contractual or other obligation to pass the dividend on to another jurisdiction. Fourth, the tax authority may grant approval and the WFOE then withholds at the 5% reduced rate; if approval is denied, 10% must be withheld and the taxpayer may challenge the decision by administrative review or administrative litigation, or use the Mutual Agreement Procedure under the DTA. The Chinese tax authority may also self-assess the application and later claw back the tax difference if the beneficial ownership or residency conditions are found false.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory CIT withholding rate for non-resident interest and royalties is 10%; under the China-Hong Kong DTA the treaty rate is 7% for both interest and royalties if the recipient is the beneficial owner and a Hong Kong resident; royalties for the right to use or distribute herbal botanical brands, know-how, or trademarks are additionally subject to PRC VAT at 6% and related surcharges unless an exemption applies; interest paid to related Hong Kong lenders must also satisfy the arm's length rate and thin capitalization rules, otherwise the excess may be re-characterized as dividend subject to 10% or 5% DWT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million for annual related-party transfers of tangible property; RMB 100 million for related-party transfers of intangible property; RMB 100 million for related-party financial asset transfers; RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions; a Master File is required when the enterprise is in a group whose annual related-party transaction volume exceeds RMB 1 billion, or when the group structure and transactions meet the thresholds in State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 42 of 2016.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC CIT Law Article 47 GAAR, the DTA beneficial ownership doctrine, and the substance-over-form principle apply; the WFOE must maintain real economic substance in China for the wholesale herbal business, including procurement contracts, inventory risk, phytosanitary quality control, shipping decisions, customer invoicing, credit risk, management decisions, and core income-generating activities; the Hong Kong shareholder must also have genuine business substance and cannot be a pure conduit shell used to access the 5% dividend rate; failure to satisfy these requirements can trigger treaty shopping re-characterization, denial of DTA benefits, full 10% withholding, and 25% CIT adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent export revenue understatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting export sales of dried goji berries to the Hong Kong parent by invoicing at artificially low prices, diverting overseas remittances to private bank accounts, inflating agricultural procurement invoices from goji cooperatives, or using false customs declarations to shift profits offshore and reduce Chinese corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63: recovery of unpaid tax plus daily late-payment surcharge and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded; Criminal Law Article 201: tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 and constituting more than 10% of the total tax due is punishable by criminal detention or up to three years imprisonment, and for especially large amounts with a proportion above 30%, seven years imprisonment plus fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under PRC Company Law Article 20 and the judicial doctrine of piercing the corporate veil, directors, shareholders, or actual controllers who abuse the limited liability form to evade CIT and WHT may be held jointly and severally liable to make good the tax loss; the legal representative and directly responsible directors may be placed on the tax exit blacklist and prohibited from leaving China under Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 44; criminal prosecution may be imposed on the supervisory and management personnel directly responsible for the fraudulent invoicing and profit shifting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and deficient contemporaneous documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dried goji berries to the Hong Kong parent below arm's length, paying excessive management, marketing, or royalty fees to an affiliated Hong Kong company, or providing intercompany loans without arm's length interest rates and without a comprehensive Local File or Master File benchmark study when statutory thresholds are exceeded; failing to file the annual Related Party Transaction Disclosure schedule with the CIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Articles 41 and 48 and the regulations under State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 42 of 2016: the tax authority may re-price the controlled transactions, adjust taxable income, impose special-tax-adjustment interest, and levy a penalty of 50% to 500% of the adjusted tax under Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 44 or 63; a special penalty may also be imposed for failing to provide contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement a transfer pricing policy with no arm's length basis and who sign or approve false intercompany agreements may be jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax and interest; the legal representative may be subjected to exit restrictions and inclusion in the serious tax violation blacklist; in cases where the TP scheme is a sham to hide taxable profits, criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 may attach to the officers who arranged the artificial pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and treaty shopping fraud in Dividend Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent has no office, hires no staff, carries no business activity, has no core income-generating activities in Hong Kong, and exists only to receive dividends from the Chinese WFOE at the reduced 5% DTA rate before immediately passing the funds to a mainland China or third-country beneficial owner; the directors submit a false beneficial ownership declaration and obtain a Tax Residency Certificate solely to abuse the China-Hong Kong DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 47 GAAR, SAT anti-treaty-shopping measures, and the DTA beneficial ownership rules: the tax authority may disregard the Hong Kong company as a conduit, deny the DTA claim, re-impose the full 10% dividend WHT, charge late-payment surcharge and special-tax-adjustment interest, and impose a 50% to 500% penalty under Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 for false declarations or withholding failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false residency and beneficial ownership certificates may be personally liable for restitution of the suppressed withholding tax; their assets may be attached if the WFOE is used as their alter ego; they face exit bans and blacklisting, and if the scheme is proven as intentional tax evasion with public prosecution, responsible officers can be sentenced to imprisonment under Criminal Law Article 201, in addition to fines and compensation for the tax loss.
